metadata.body:
# PoroTomo Induced-Seismicity Agent

Blueprint for clio-agent. The numeric work lives in plain scripts in this
repository so it can run on PBS compute nodes without an LLM:

- `agent/manifest.py`: list the DASV records on `s3://nrel-pds-porotomo/` and sample them.
- `agent/detect.py`: per-record detector (common-mode removal, 10-150 Hz band-pass, median STA/LTA).
- `agent/pbs/submit.sh`: submit the distributed detection plus aggregation job to Aurora.
- `agent/hazard.py`: anomaly z-scores, event catalogue, pumping volumes, seismogenic index, probabilities.

The experts orchestrate those scripts, inspect files, and explain results. They
never make up numbers. Every figure they report comes from `summary.json` or a
tool result.

Install by linking this directory into `~/.config/clio-agent/agent-blueprints/`.

agent_blueprint.name: PoroTomo Induced-Seismicity Agent

session.title: porotomo-induced-seismicity: Report the headline results of the agent

answer:
Headline results of the read-only agent run (no PBS jobs submitted, hazard.py not run by me — the numbers below are quoted from the run's own artifacts):

Run directory: /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (run id run_20261115T155359Z_s20; summary.json generated 2026-11-15T16:02:33+00:00; original PBS job 9092130.aurora-pbs-0001.hostmgmt.cm.aurora.alcf.anl.gov, 2 nodes x 24 ranks = 48 ranks).

Records analysed: 759 (all status ok; stride 20 out of 15,164 total PoroTomo iDAS .h5 records, DAS/H5/DASV/20160317 through 20160326; first 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z, last 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z; sampled_fraction_of_time 0.0331; mean 2003.99 ms per record).

Anomalous records: 57 (z_threshold 5.0); strongest anomaly 2016-03-23T20:50:17Z, zmax 30.92 (driver max_sta_lta).

DAS detections: 62 events (n_scaled_to_full_time 1870.77; 53 records with events; relative b = 0.9849352475487246, mc_relative -0.8492463451632817, 34 above mc).

Seismogenic index Sigma (catalog-based, per b scenario):
- b = 1.0: Sigma = -5.448901270028832
- b = 0.73: Sigma = -5.3193012700288325
- b = 0.65: Sigma = -5.280901270028833
(The DAS upper bound instead uses Sigma = -2.698279919032152 with b_used = 0.9849352475487246, b_source "DAS relative-magnitude Aki MLE".)

P(Mw >= 5.5) per year at the observed rate, catalog-based (CALIBRATED — source "GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016", calibrated ML, n=5, mc -0.48, mag_max 0.07):
- b = 1.0: 0.00011982478978644906 (~1.2e-4 /yr)
- b = 0.73: 0.004921548824626587 (~4.9e-3 /yr)
- b = 0.65: 0.014735103451029574 (~1.5e-2 /yr)
(Over the observed volume instead: 5.235629034316958e-06, 0.00021553767643867072, 0.0006483793467004784 respectively.)

DAS-based upper bound on P(Mw >= 5.5) per year: 0.07842182774171746 (~7.8e-2 /yr; over observed volume 0.0024076054468051833). This is an UPPER BOUND ONLY, not calibrated: it treats every DAS detection as an event at/above the catalogue minimum magnitude with uncalibrated (relative) magnitudes, so it over-counts.

Which is which: the catalog-based probabilities (b = 1.0 / 0.73 / 0.65) are the calibrated set, resting on the LBNL/NCEDC March 2016 catalogue (GDR 859) with calibrated local magnitudes. The DAS-based 0.07842182774171746 is an uncalibrated upper bound resting on DAS relative magnitudes (Aki MLE b = 0.9849) and the assumption that each DAS detection counts as a catalog-minimum-or-larger event. A Pohang-like Mw >= 5.5 event in one year is therefore at most ~7.8% by the conservative DAS bound, and ~0.012%–1.47% per year across the calibrated b scenarios (1.2e-4 at b=1.0 up to 1.47e-2 at b=0.65).

Assumptions each rests on: records analysed assume the stride-20 sample (759 of 15,164) is representative; anomalies use z_threshold 5.0 on the max_sta_lta driver; Sigma and the catalog probabilities assume the GDR 859 LBNL/NCEDC catalogue Gutenberg-Richter fit (mc -0.48) applies over the observed volume and rate; the DAS upper bound additionally assumes uncalibrated DAS detections can be mapped to catalogue magnitudes at/above mc, which is why it is quoted only as an upper bound. Caveat noted in the run logs: 6 transient download failures were retried (retry_manifest.txt) and the final summary counts all 759 records as ok.
